interactions.teaches: Rotating the three-plane assembly reveals that space is divided into eight wedges (octants), including the one hidden behind the sheets in the static figure — the 3D analog of the four quadrants of the plane

Hovering a wedge brightens that octant and enlarges its (+/−) triple, showing that each sign is fixed by which side of the corresponding coordinate plane the region lies on: first sign = side of the yz-plane, second = side of the xz-plane, third = side of the xy-plane

interactions.label: Emphasized plane
interactions.teaches: Highlighting one coordinate plane recolors the two half-spaces it separates, clarifying that crossing that one plane flips exactly one coordinate sign while the other two stay fixed

demo_steps.title: Three planes, eight regions
demo_steps.narration: The three translucent coordinate planes meet at the origin and cut space into eight octants, just as two axes cut the plane into four quadrants. Octant I, where all three coordinates are positive, sits in the near upper wedge.

demo_steps.title: The xy-plane splits z
demo_steps.narration: With the horizontal xy-plane emphasized, the half-space above (z > 0) and below (z < 0) recolor. Every upper region has a partner directly beneath it — e.g. (+, +, +) sits above (+, +, −) — only the third sign changes.

demo_steps.title: The yz-plane splits x
demo_steps.narration: Now the peach yz-plane (x = 0) is emphasized. Crossing from the front half-space to the back flips only the first sign: (+, +, +) becomes (−, +, +).

demo_steps.title: The xz-plane splits y
demo_steps.narration: Finally the blue-violet xz-plane (y = 0) is emphasized. Crossing from right to left flips only the second sign: (+, +, +) becomes (+, −, +). Hover the wedges to read each octant's triple, including the hidden (−, −, −).

plan.geometry_notes: WORLD CONVENTION: z is vertical (+Z = screen-up), +Y points screen-right, +X points toward the viewer / lower-left. All octant sign triples are ordered (x, y, z) and positioned in this z-up frame. Axes span ±3 world units with arrowheads at the positive ends. Origin at (0,0,0). Three plane sheets, each ~6 × 6 units, centered at the origin: xy-plane horizontal (normal +Z), teal #7fc4c4 at ~0.45 opacity; yz-plane vertical containing the y- and z-axes (normal +X), peach #f4b183 at ~0.45 opacity; xz-plane vertical containing the x- and z-axes (normal +Y), blue-violet #8e9bcc at ~0.45 opacity. Axis segments hidden behind a sheet render dashed. LABEL PLACEMENT (z-up): the 'z' axis label sits just right of the upper z-arrow tip; the (−, −, +) label is placed deep in the back upper wedge at roughly (x≈−2.0, y≈−2.0, z≈1.6), clearly separated from the z-axis and its label. Octant I (+,+,+) is the wedge x>0, y>0, z>0 (near upper); its bold 'I' floats at roughly (x≈1.6, y≈1.6, z≈1.8) with the '(+, +, +)' triple ~0.5 units beneath it, keeping both well clear of the origin and axes. Other labels centered in their wedges at ~2 units from each plane. Each octant region is a 2×2×2 cube occupying its wedge for hover highlighting; the (−,−,−) octant (x<0, y<0, z<0) sits diagonally opposite Octant I, hidden behind the sheets in the default view. Labels: black text, triples like (+, −, +).
plan.notes: Three.js default is y-up: either build the scene z-up and set camera.up to (0,0,1), or keep a root group rotation so the world z-axis renders vertical — do NOT reassign which sheet is horizontal. Render plane sheets with MeshLambertMaterial, transparent: true, side: DoubleSide, depthWrite: false so the three translucencies composite cleanly. Dashed axis portions: THREE.LineDashedMaterial with computeLineDistances. Octant hover targets: eight invisible box meshes (2×2×2) per octant; on hover, raise that box's opacity to ~0.25 in a warm highlight and show an enlarged sign-triple sprite near the axes. For plane emphasis, tint the emphasized sheet more saturated and recolor the octant boxes on its two sides in contrasting warm vs cool tints while other sheets fade. Keep axis labels ('x', 'y', 'z') as sprites pinned to arrow tips with screen-space offsets so they never overlap the (−, −, +) wedge label.

authoredPrompt: This figure is a three-dimensional coordinate diagram assembled from three translucent coordinate planes that cut space apart. The vertical axis is labeled z, the axis running to the right is labeled y, and the axis coming forward toward the lower left is labeled x. A pale teal horizontal sheet represents the xy-plane, a peach-colored vertical sheet stretches across the width of the picture, and a blue-violet vertical sheet crosses it at a right angle, all three meeting at the origin. Text set into the wedges between the planes gives the sign pattern of the coordinates there: the near upper wedge carries a bold roman numeral I above the triple (+, +, +), and the surrounding regions are marked (-, -, +), (+, -, +), (-, +, +), (-, +, -), (+, -, -), and (+, +, -), the eighth region being hidden behind the sheets. Portions of the axes drawn as dashed lines indicate where they pass behind a plane. Labeling each region by its signs lets the reader read off directly which side of every coordinate plane that region lies on. The picture carries the familiar division of the plane into four quadrants over into the division of space into eight octants.
authoredInteractions:
- Hover for octant sign patterns: the learner hovers a wedge, that region brightens and its (+/-) triple expands next to the axes, showing that each coordinate sign is determined by which side of the corresponding coordinate plane the point lies on.
- Toggle between plane emphasis modes: the learner switches among xy-plane, xz-plane, and yz-plane highlights, and the two sign-changing half-spaces recolor, clarifying how crossing one plane changes exactly one coordinate sign.
authoredContext:
In two dimensions, the coordinate axes partition the plane into four quadrants. Similarly, the coordinate planes divide space between them into eight regions about the origin, called octants. The octants fill ℝ3 in the same way that quadrants fill ℝ2, as shown in the figure.

Points that lie in octants have three nonzero coordinates.

This figure is the 3-dimensional coordinate system with the first octant labeled with a roman numeral I, I, II, III, IV, V, VI, VII, and VIII. Also, for each quadrant there are the signs of the values of x, y, and z. They are: I (+, +, +); 2nd (-, +, +); 3rd (-, -, +); 4th (+, -, +); 5th (+, +, -); 6th (-, +, -); 7th (-, -, -); and 8th (+, -, -).

Most work in three-dimensional space is a comfortable extension of the corresponding concepts in two dimensions. In this section, we use our knowledge of circles to describe spheres, then we expand our understanding of vectors to three dimensions. To accomplish these goals, we begin by adapting the distance formula to three-dimensional space.

LABEL PLACEMENT (z-up): the 'z' axis label sits just right of the upper z-arrow tip; the (−, −, +) label is placed deep in the back upper wedge at roughly (x≈−2.0, y≈−2.0, z≈1.6), clearly separated from the z-axis and its label. Octant I (+,+,+) is the wedge x>0, y>0, z>0 (near upper); its bold 'I' floats at roughly (x≈1.6, y≈1.6, z≈1.8) with the '(+, +, +)' triple ~0.5 units beneath it, keeping both well clear of the origin and axes. Other labels centered in their wedges at ~2 units from each plane. Each octant region is a 2×2×2 cube occupying its wedge for hover highlighting; the (−,−,−) octant (x<0, y<0, z<0) sits diagonally opposite Octant I, hidden behind the sheets in the default view. Labels: black text, triples like (+, −, +).
plan.notes: Three.js default is y-up: either build the scene z-up and set camera.up to (0,0,1), or keep a root group rotation so the world z-axis renders vertical — do NOT reassign which sheet is horizontal. Render plane sheets with MeshLambertMaterial, transparent: true, side: DoubleSide, depthWrite: false so the three translucencies composite cleanly. Dashed axis portions: THREE.LineDashedMaterial with computeLineDistances. Octant hover targets: eight invisible box meshes (2×2×2) per octant; on hover, raise that box's opacity to ~0.25 in a warm highlight and show an enlarged sign-triple sprite near the axes. For plane emphasis, tint the emphasized sheet more saturated and recolor the octant boxes on its two sides in contrasting warm vs cool tints while other sheets fade. Keep axis labels ('x', 'y', 'z') as sprites pinned to arrow tips with screen-space offsets so they never overlap the (−, −, +) wedge label.
